<!-- pr-reviewer: fb1ac45824660f56fec848f1ed802a06f90efb39 -->
Review of #2664, head fb1ac4582. Built in a worktree: the head merged with current main (clean), then the import suites and clippy ran.

Result: pass. No blockers.

What was run:
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test tilted_gouge --test import --test import_bytes --test import_outward --test import_step_closed_shell --test fixture_step_library --test fidelity_copies` - 7 binaries, 48 tests, all pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` - clean.

What the review checked:
- `step_fit.rs`: the red-green split keeps the two facets that share an inside edge conforming. All eight split patterns keep the winding. A boundary edge is never split, so the shell stays closed.
- The vertex guard (line 127) refuses a mesh whose parameters do not give its points. The face is then left as the kernel made it.
- The chord error `off` flows to `kept.tol.max(off)` and then to `coarse()`. A mesh that cannot be refined gets reduced fidelity, and the verify gate refuses it. This matches the module header.
- The split vertices are always on the surface. A non-finite surface point is not added and is reported as `off`.
- The budget accounting is correct: `room` is the facets left in the pass, and the `Over` check runs after each face.
- `testdata/models/bar_cross_holes.step` is an original SolidCraft export. The provenance comment names only public sources (Ericson-free: the elementary sagitta and the Bank-Sherman-Weiser and Rivara split rules).

P1 floor: second review needed. This change decides what every gouge law sees for a STEP part with a hole in a curved wall. It fixes #2600 (P1). A read-only second review on the Opus model is required before the merge.

Note for the merge: the reported bar grows from about 1 084 facets to about 133 000, and its import takes about 5 s in a debug build. A correct kernel mesh is not changed.

Second review (Opus, read-only, not built) of head fb1ac45824660f56fec848f1ed802a06f90efb39.

Verdict: CLEAN. I found no blocker. The PR is already merged (merge commit c49d36762, 2026-11-19T05:15Z). Thus each finding below is a follow-up.

## What I checked

1. Diagnosis. The diagnosis is sound. Before the fix, the wall facets of the imported bar ran up to 25 mm inside the true cylinder. Each gouge law judged against that mesh. The guard test `a_tilted_slot_into_a_meshed_bar_is_refused` shows that the keep law convicts a tilted slot on a correct mesh. The pin `a_tilted_slot_into_the_step_bar_is_refused` asserts a refusal (a `Gouge` warning on each slot, the post error "cuts past the finish surface", and no file). The PR body gives the red output of the two pins on unchanged code.
2. Termination. The split loop has at most 25 rounds (`ROUNDS`, `step_fit.rs:58`, `:143`). Each round stops when it makes more facets than `room` (`:180`). A non-finite surface point makes no vertex, and its height goes into `off` as infinity (`:166-167`). An infinite chord is refused as a corrupt import at `step.rs` (`parse_open`, the `chord.is_finite()` check). Thus a corrupt face gives a clean error, not a hang and not a silent pass.
3. Topology. I read the eight split patterns (`step_fit.rs:197-208`). Each keeps the winding of its parent facet. A split is keyed by the edge only, so the two facets of an inside edge split at the same vertex. No T-junction is possible inside a face. An edge with one facet (a face boundary, or a seam with two parameter values) is never split, so no T-junction is possible between two faces. A non-manifold edge (three or more facets) is also left alone.
4. Units. `tol`, `off` and the positions are all in the file unit. `kept.tol.max(off)` is scaled by `mm_per_unit` with the rest of the chord. This is correct.
5. Measure. For a cylinder and a sphere, the distance from a chord to the surface has its maximum at the chord midpoint. The measure (chord midpoint to the surface point at the parameter midpoint) is not smaller than that distance. Thus it is an upper bound along the edge for these two kinds. For a cone and a torus, it is only an estimate; see F1.
6. Code shape. No `unwrap()`, `expect()` or `panic!()` in the new source. `step_fit.rs` has 209 lines and a provenance comment that names public sources. `step.rs` has 400 lines, at the limit. No new crate dependency. The decision entry `docs/decisions/2600-step-facets-on-surface.md` is present. No process file, snapshot PNG, `CHANGELOG.md` or `RECOMMENDED.md` changes.
7. Fixture. `testdata/models/bar_cross_holes.step` has 56 236 bytes. Its header names SolidCraft as the originating system. It has no Autodesk or third-party marks.

## Follow-ups (not blockers)

- F1 (proposed P3). The reported chord can be smaller than the measured mesh error. `step_fit.rs:55` and `:162` keep an inside edge that stands up to `SLACK` x `tol` (2 x 0.005 = 0.01 mm) off the surface. `step.rs:399` then reports `kept.tol` (0.005 mm) when nothing stays over that limit. Also, the edge measure does not include the facet interior. On a sphere, the interior of a facet can stand about 4/3 of its edge height off the surface. On a cone or a torus, the edge midpoint is not exactly the maximum. The worst case is a convex wall that is about 0.013 mm inside the true surface, while the import reports 0.005 mm. This is less than the error before the fix by orders of magnitude, and it is near `DEV_TOL`. It is not a blocker. Recommended fix: report the largest measured height of the kept inside edges, not only the height over the limit.
- F2 (proposed P3). A face that fails the parameter check falls back silently. `step_fit.rs:113-130` returns `KEPT` for a non-triangle face, a missing parameter, or a vertex more than `tol * 1e-3` from its surface point. There is no log. If a different STEP writer causes this fallback, the defect of #2600 comes back without a diagnostic. Recommended: log the fallback with the face index, and add a test that pins it.
- F3 (proposed P3, an audit). The second half of #2600 is not closed by this PR. The stock sim still does not judge posed moves, and `verify` still answers `ok: true` with `not_judged`. The PR depends on the generation-time keep law. The pins show this law only for `Slot`. Recommended: audit each operation kind that accepts a `Tilt` for a generation-time gouge law. A kind without one is a P1.
- F4 (proposed P6). Facet count and time. The reported bar grows from 1 084 to about 133 000 facets (about 5 s in debug). The fit runs on each pass of the tolerance schedule. The facet budget bounds the growth, so there is no unbounded cost. But a part with many cross holes in curved walls can use all of the budget. It then imports at reduced fidelity, and the gate refuses it. Repeated single-edge splits also make thin facets. The better triangulation (interior rows, or a parameter stretch for elementary faces) is the follow-up that the decision entry names.
- F5 (proposed P7). Missing tests: the fallback path (budget or round cap reached, then `off` is reported and the model has reduced fidelity), and a cone, sphere or torus face with a hole. The wall pin allows 0.02 mm (`tilted_gouge.rs`, `R - 0.02`). That is four times `CHORD_CAP`. A limit of `SLACK * CHORD_CAP` pins the law more closely.
- F6 (proposed P7). Crate placement. `step_fit.rs` reads no ECS world, project file, command, MCP or CLI. By the rule "app holds the document", it belongs in a domain crate. It depends on `step_guard::Metered` and on the truck STEP importer family, which are in `crates/app` before this PR. Thus a move of this file alone is not practical. It is not a blocker. Move it when the STEP mesher family moves.
- F7 (housekeeping). The PR merged before the first review (06:07Z) and before this second review. Issue #2600 is closed but still has the `in-review` label.
